page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6.26xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware resources include 104 dedicated vCPUs powered by Intel Xeon 8269CY processors running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. Hypervisor management is handled via KVM. The instance provides 768 GB of system RAM, resulting in approximately 7.38 GB of memory per core, which accommodates large footprint memory residency.

The hardware configuration contains no local storage and does not include discrete GPU accelerators. Consequently, all persistent disk input and output rely on external network-attached volumes. Network connectivity is rated at a 25 Gbps baseline bandwidth, facilitating consistent data transmission between the instance and networked storage or distributed services.

Resource allocation focuses heavily on the balance between high core counts and deep memory capacity. This design enables high consolidation of services that would otherwise span multiple smaller nodes, reducing network overhead in scale-up architectures. Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6.26xlarge is suited for in-memory caching platforms, enterprise relational databases, large-scale data mining, and in-memory analytics frameworks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6.26xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud instance built on the x86_64 architecture and managed by the KVM hypervisor. It features 104 dedicated vCPUs powered by Intel Xeon 8269CY processors operating at 2.5 GHz, alongside 768 GB of system memory. This yields a dense memory allocation of roughly 7.38 GB per core. The server includes no local storage drives and zero discrete GPUs, relying on connected network block volumes for persistent data storage and high-speed data access via a 25 Gbps baseline network interface. Configured for workloads that require significant memory footprints and strong multithreaded capacity without graphic acceleration, the ecs.r6.26xlarge instance serves enterprise deployments such as in-memory databases, distributed caches, real-time analytics engines, and large database systems.
